- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows strong bearish momentum, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–2% from forecast for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model frequently underestimates true price peaks in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for 10–15 day window if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead of actual price movement.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; if sentiment turns bullish late (last 3–5 days), increase forecast by 1–2% for final 5–7 days.
